Decant

A benchmark-first toolkit for ambient RNA decontamination research in single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq. Decant is assembled from components, and a component becomes a default ONLY after it passes a falsification gate against ground truth. This is not a finished CellBender replacement and does not claim to be one. Its value is that every capability in it has been shown to earn its place, and the things that did not are documented as failures.

“Decant” is a working placeholder name. Check CRAN, Bioconductor, and GitHub for collisions before any release.

Install and run 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("kroy3/Decant")

On real 10x data (the RAW matrix is required: the empty droplets are the soup measurement):

library(Decant)
raw  <- read_10x_counts("sample/outs/raw_feature_bc_matrix")
cell_bcs <- colnames(read_10x_counts("sample/outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix"))
d    <- split_droplets(raw, cells = cell_bcs)       # cells vs empty droplets
res  <- decant(d$cells, d$empties, clusters = my_seurat_clusters)
res                       # summary, including any warnings about rho reliability
res$corrected             # corrected counts, still a sparse dgCMatrix
res$rho_diagnostics       # per-cluster rho, absent-gene power, borrowing

From a Seurat object 

obj <- RunDecant(obj, raw = "sample/outs/raw_feature_bc_matrix")
obj <- NormalizeData(obj, assay = "Decant")   # then your usual workflow
obj$decant_rho                                # per-cell contamination
Misc(obj, "decant")$rho_diagnostics           # per-cluster reliability

RunDecant() uses your Idents() as clusters and writes the corrected counts to a new Decant assay, leaving RNA untouched. It handles the bookkeeping that usually breaks this step. Seurat renames _ to - in gene names, so the raw matrix is renamed the same way. Barcodes prefixed by merge(add.cell.ids=) or suffixed by integration are matched back to the raw matrix, and every cell must match or it stops with examples. Split v5 layers are joined. Normalised or SCTransformed data is refused, because Decant needs raw UMI counts. For a merged multi-sample object, pass one raw matrix per sample:

obj <- RunDecant(obj, raw = list(A = "A/raw_feature_bc_matrix",
                                 B = "B/raw_feature_bc_matrix"),
                 sample_col = "sample")

Pass your own clusters (Seurat / SCE) when you have them; otherwise k-means is run. Inputs may be dense matrices or Matrix::dgCMatrix. Sparse inputs stay sparse end to end: a 20k-gene x 20k-cell sparse matrix (229 MB) runs in ~10-20 s at ~1.1 GB peak, where v0.1 needed a 3 GB dense intermediate.

The design rule

Earlier work in this repo established, against ground truth, that putting a smarter model on the same count matrix (a fancier soup profile) does not move the sensitivity/specificity frontier. So every module here brings in ORTHOGONAL information to break the ambient-vs-native identifiability problem, and each is gated. Run the scorecard yourself (~1 min):

Rscript run_all_gates.R

Scorecard (from run_all_gates.R, v0.2)

Core components (every run depends on these)

Component Gate result Default
Contamination fraction (rho): cluster-pooled absent-gene estimator with empirical-Bayes per-cell shrinkage (estimate_rho_cluster) PASS on 12 settings (easy + stress simulator, rho 0 to 0.3, k-means clusters, not oracle). Mean bias within 25% everywhere; negative control holds (rho=0 gives <0.01). Easy: RMSE 0.006-0.030, per-cell r = 0.94-0.98. Stress: RMSE 0.03-0.08, r = 0.50-0.81. ON
Legacy marker-ratio rho (v0.1 estimate_rho) FAIL. Overestimated rho 1.5-4x on easy data (worst at the low rho typical of scRNA-seq) and reported 0.57-0.71 when the truth was 0.0-0.3 under stress. kept only for reproducibility
Correction rule On simulated data subtract (v0) has the lowest mean L1 error (0.071), vs redistribute (SoupX-style, 0.073) and bayes (0.076); none dominates. On real PBMC data bayes removed 83 to 94% of foreign marker counts against 19 to 57% for subtract, at the same cost to native expression. bayes (decided by the real data, against the simulated gate); others via correction=

What the rho fix buys end to end (compare_methods.R, mean of 4 seeds, L1 error to the clean truth, lower is better):

true rho no correction v0.1 pipeline v0.2 decant()
0.1 0.109 0.147 (worse than doing nothing) 0.042
0.3 0.426 0.176 0.101

At rho=0.1 the v0.1 pipeline destroyed 12.5% of real signal through over-correction.

Modules

Gap Module Gate result Default
1 Splice-aware layer decontamination PASS. Cuts unspliced-layer error by 25% (0.044 vs 0.059) when ambient is splice-distinct. Ties exactly when it is not (negative control holds). Outputs corrected spliced/unspliced layers for RNA velocity. ON
3 Hierarchical multi-sample soup pooling PASS. Reduces soup error for empty-poor samples; neutral for empty-rich. ON
5 Allelic / genotype-aware rho PASS. Near-ground-truth rho in pooled designs. (Gate contrast is soft, 0.015 vs 0.017 RMSE; the absolute accuracy is the real point.) ON when allelic data present
4 Structured-soup lysis diagnostic PASS as QC only, with an oracle basis. It is a diagnostic readout, never a corrector (that use was falsified). ON as diagnostic
2 Decontamination-aware DE, v1 (ambient load as a log-scale covariate) FAIL. 90% false positives on ambient-trap genes, 16% on null genes. OFF, superseded
2 Contamination-aware DE, v2 (ambient_de(), DecantDE()) PASS (gate_ambient_de). 0 leaked genes called in every case, against 17-57 for standard edgeR pseudobulk; null false-positive rate 0.048-0.056; power kept, including on genes truly DE in both cell types. ON

Contamination-aware differential expression

When ambient RNA differs between samples (fragile disease tissue lyses more), standard pseudobulk DE reports an abundant cell type’s disease genes as DE in rare cell types. Correcting counts with Decant’s default subtract rule and then testing does not stop this (about half of the leaked genes are still called, see the comparator table below). Official SoupX followed by edgeR does remove almost all of it on the simulator, so “correct first” is not a lost cause in general. DecantDE() takes the other route and models each sample’s measured soup inside the test:

res <- DecantDE(obj, cell_type = "Microglia", sample_col = "donor",
                formula = ~ diagnosis, raw = raw_paths_by_donor)
subset(res, FDR < 0.05)        # contamination-aware hits
subset(res, ambient_driven)    # standard-pipeline hits explained by soup

The model: negative binomial with mean native + ambient, where the ambient term is each sample’s own soup (from its empty droplets, shrunk by empirical Bayes only as far as its noise warrants), scaled by an ambient fraction re-estimated from the target cell type’s own pseudobulk. The soup’s sampling variance enters the variance, TMM handles composition, and a quasi-likelihood F-test keeps small-sample tests calibrated. ambient_de() takes plain pseudobulk matrices.

Results of gate_ambient_de() (6 vs 6 samples, contamination ~5% vs 12%):

case leaked genes called (naive / Decant) null FP (naive / Decant) FDP (naive / Decant)
more soup in disease 56.5 / 0 0.246 / 0.048 0.84 / 0.15
equal soup, disease-shifted composition 17.0 / 0 0.061 / 0.056 0.40 / 0.07
genes truly DE in both types 31.5 / 0 0.235 / 0.049 0.72 / 0.10

Against correct-then-test with the official tools

validation/de_comparators.R corrects each sample with a tool, pseudobulks the rare type, and runs edgeR QL. Mean of 4 seeds, 6 vs 6 samples, same scoring as the gate. Every corrector gets the true cell-type labels.

case method leaked genes called null FP power FDP
more soup in disease naive edgeR 52.8 / 80 0.223 0.91 0.82
ambient_de 0 / 80 0.048 0.92 0.13
Decant bayes (default) + edgeR 0 / 80 0.045 0.89 0.11
Decant redistribute + edgeR 6.0 / 80 0.081 0.90 0.31
SoupX + edgeR 1.5 / 80 0.043 0.85 0.13
equal soup, shifted composition naive edgeR 12.5 / 80 0.060 0.92 0.35
ambient_de 0 / 80 0.051 0.94 0.11
Decant bayes (default) + edgeR 0 / 80 0.051 0.94 0.10
Decant redistribute + edgeR 0.5 / 80 0.060 0.94 0.12
SoupX + edgeR 0.25 / 80 0.042 0.89 0.09
genes truly DE in both types naive edgeR 30.8 / 60 0.227 0.92 0.71
ambient_de 0 / 60 0.057 0.97 0.11
Decant bayes (default) + edgeR 0 / 60 0.045 0.95 0.09
Decant redistribute + edgeR 9.0 / 60 0.114 0.94 0.43
SoupX + edgeR 2.3 / 60 0.051 0.90 0.14

What this says, including the parts that do not favour Decant:

  • Correcting with Decant’s bayes rule and then running edgeR is as good as ambient_de here. It calls no leaked gene, is calibrated, and has a slightly lower false discovery proportion. ambient_de has 0 to 3 points more power. In this 6 vs 6 two-group simulation, modelling the ambient term inside the test buys almost nothing over a good correction. (With the earlier subtract default, correct-then-test called 41.5 of 80 leaked genes; that gap was the correction rule, not the testing strategy.)
  • SoupX + edgeR is close on leakage and FDP, with 4 to 7 points less power and 0.25 to 2.3 leaked genes called. That is a modest margin on a simulator that matches Decant’s own assumptions.
  • SoupX’s autoEstCont found no marker genes at its defaults on every sample of this simulator. It was rerun with soupQuantile = 0.5, the remedy its own error message gives. The rule is fixed and not tuned to the truth.
  • DecontX, FastCAR and CellBender were not run (not installed where this table was produced). The wrappers are in validation/comparators.R; the FastCAR and CellBender wrappers have never been executed. See validation/README.md.
  • Where ambient_de is still expected to matter is outside this table: when the ambient estimate is noisy enough that its uncertainty has to enter the test (few empties, few cells), and at small sample sizes with covariates. Neither has been compared against bayes + edgeR yet.

Large cohorts, outlier samples and covariates

NB tests lose false-positive control in population-scale cohorts when a few samples carry extreme counts (Li et al. 2022, Genome Biology 23:79), and ambient_de() did too. It now down-weights outlier samples per gene (robust = TRUE, the default), and gate_ambient_de_cohort() checks it in CI. Null false-positive rate at a nominal 0.05, mean of 3 seeds:

per group case ambient_de without down-weighting naive edgeR naive Wilcoxon subtract + Wilcoxon
50 clean 0.056 0.052 0.382 0.369 0.054
50 1% outlier entries 0.053 0.335 0.444 0.366 0.053
50 heavy-tailed noise 0.044 0.146 0.303 0.267 0.047
50 confounding batch 0.050 0.044 0.451 0.462 0.141
200 clean 0.064 0.057 0.759 0.738 0.053
200 confounding batch 0.056 0.050 0.764 0.741 0.213
  • A rank test does not fix contamination: naive Wilcoxon is as inflated as naive edgeR when contamination differs between groups.
  • In a two-group design with 50 or more per group, subtracting the ambient estimate and then running Wilcoxon is as good as ambient_de.
  • ambient_de is the better choice below about 50 per group (power 0.86 vs 0.61 at 15) and when a covariate must be adjusted for: with a confounding batch the rank test’s false discovery proportion is 0.64 to 0.85.
  • From 50 per group up, ambient_de’s false discovery proportion at a nominal 0.10 is 0.10 to 0.17, from genes with very small residual shifts. lfc = log2(1.1) tests against a 10% minimum fold change and removed them with no loss of power for 1.5-fold effects.
  • Genes whose counts are more than 75% ambient are not tested; they are listed in attr(res, "ambient_dominated").

The sweep over 6 to 200 per group is in experiments/large_cohort_calibration/.

Limits: - With very few empty droplets (150) some leakage returns. - With 3 samples per group, power drops (0.58 vs 0.68 for naive). - The base case’s false discovery proportion (0.15) sits exactly at the gate’s threshold. - All results are simulated, from a simulator built around the mechanism the model assumes. The full development history, including the variants that were rejected, is in experiments/contamination_aware_de/.

Corrections to v0.1 claims

This release re-ran every gate on the shipped estimator. Three earlier claims did not survive, and they are corrected here rather than quietly edited:

  1. “Splice-aware halves unspliced-layer error.” The 2x came partly from the legacy rho over-correcting the baseline more heavily. With a calibrated rho the gain is 25%, and the negative control initially FAILED because each layer was clamped separately (losing removal mass twice). Fixed by clamping the total once and routing overflow between layers. The control now ties.
  2. “DE: the problem is real and severe.” The v0.1 DE benchmark was broken. It renormalised condition B after up-regulating the true-DE genes, and compared plain CPM, so naive DE called 58% of NULL genes significant. With median-of-ratios normalisation the benchmark is calibrated (7% null FP), and naive subtract-then-test has only 8% FP on ambient-trap genes when given the true ambient load. With the ambient load estimated and soups differing between samples (the realistic case, gate_ambient_de), leakage is severe, which is what the v2 contamination-aware test addresses.
  3. “Default rho estimator overestimates ~2x.” It was 1.5-4x, and catastrophically worse under realistic heterogeneity. Replaced (see above).

Known limitations (stated, not hidden)

  • Empties that do not match the cells make rho collapse (partly handled). Genes that are in the empties but in no cell at all are now detected and dropped from the soup, with a warning when they exceed 5% of it. Genes the cells do contain but the empties over-represent (debris of an under-sampled cell type) are not detected: the estimator settles on them and rho is underestimated. In simulation, 10% such junk took a true rho of 0.2 to 0.005. Earlier versions carried a two-sided tripwire for this case, which caught 20 of 22 simulated runs. It raised a false alarm on the real PBMC data and has been retired; the per-cluster two-sided estimate is still in $rho_diagnostics. Check a suspiciously low rho against marker genes.
  • Weak identifiability when few genes are cleanly absent. When cell types share most of their expression program, rho is not identifiable from counts alone and the estimator biases UP (~+10% under stress). Clusters with almost no absent genes borrow the evidence-weighted rho of the others and are flagged low_power. Per-cell resolution is limited (r = 0.5-0.8 under stress).
  • Over-clustering biases rho up. Very small clusters lack the power to reject weakly-expressed genes. Prefer a moderate number of reasonably large clusters.
  • The DecontX-like comparator is not a fair stand-in for DecontX. It removes only ~8-10% of contamination here, which says more about the reimplementation than about DecontX. There is no SoupX reimplementation at all. Nothing here is a claim against either tool.
  • The lysis diagnostic was validated with an oracle basis; real k-means clustering degrades it.
  • All results are on simulated data. Simulations can be rigged. These are sufficiency tests and negative controls, not evidence against CellBender. The stress simulator exists because the original one made rho estimation too easy.

Real-data validation (in progress)

PBMC 4k (run)

validation/pbmc_soupx.R runs decant() on the 10x PBMC data bundled with SoupX: 2,150 annotated cells, 33,694 genes, a soup profile from 2.7M empty-droplet UMIs. There is no ground truth, so the checks are indirect.

This run found a serious bug. The rho estimator as released gave a median of 0.22 (up to 0.58 in small clusters) where SoupX’s own analyses of the same data give 0.06 (automatic) and 0.077 (immunoglobulin genes). Tens of thousands of low-count genes passed the “not significantly above the soup” test for lack of power and dragged rho up; the simulators, with 300 to 2,000 well-covered genes, never showed it. The absent set now requires an expected ambient count of at least 5 (min_expected).

check result
rho, median / mean over cells 0.063 / 0.076 (SoupX: 0.06 automatic, 0.077 from IG genes)
immunoglobulin counts in non-B cells explained by rho x soup 94%
monocyte marker counts (LYZ, S100A8, S100A9) in non-monocytes explained 106%
NK markers (GNLY, NKG7) outside NK and CD8 T explained 92%

Share of those foreign marker counts removed, and of the same genes’ counts in the cell type that expresses them:

correction IG foreign IG native monocyte foreign monocyte native NK foreign NK native
bayes 0.86 0.01 0.94 0.04 0.83 0.02
redistribute 0.27 0.01 0.73 0.05 0.35 0.02
subtract 0.19 0.01 0.57 0.04 0.24 0.01

decant() now defaults to correction = "bayes". The simulated gate_correction() still puts the three rules within a few percent of each other with subtract marginally ahead; the real data does not.

Limits: one dataset, one tissue, no ground truth, and agreement with SoupX is agreement with another estimator, not with the truth. Three of eleven clusters (the monocyte clusters, which dominate the soup) could not identify their own rho and borrowed it. The two-sided soup/cell mismatch tripwire raised a false alarm on this data and was retired (see Known limitations).

Species mixtures (not yet run)

validation/species_mix.R scores Decant on public 10x human/mouse mixtures (hgmm_1k_v3, hgmm_5k_v3, hgmm_10k_v3), where every cross-species read is known contamination, so rho is measured experimentally instead of simulated. It runs the OFFICIAL SoupX and DecontX when they are installed (never the in-repo reimplementations), and reports each missing comparator as “not run”.

Rscript validation/species_mix.R              # all datasets
Rscript validation/species_mix.R hgmm_1k_v3   # one dataset

Two tests per dataset:

  • full: all cells, both genomes. Comparable to published benchmarks, but easy for absent-gene estimators, because the other genome is a perfect set of absent genes. A good score here alone shows little.
  • hidden: majority-species cells with that species’ genes only. The estimator has to work as it would on ordinary single-species data, while the truth still comes from the cross-species reads it cannot see. This is the test that matters.

The truth derivation is unit-tested on a synthetic mixture with known rho (it recovers the mean within 0.01). No real-data numbers are reported yet: the datasets have not been run. Downloads need network access to cf.10xgenomics.com. Alternatively, place the extracted raw_feature_bc_matrix/ and filtered_feature_bc_matrix/ folders under validation/data/<dataset>/raw/ and validation/data/<dataset>/filtered/.

The non-negotiable next step

Nothing here is a real-world claim until it is re-run on experimental ground truth: species-mixing (human/mouse, e.g. 10x hgmm) and genotype-mixing (demuxlet/souporcell-style) datasets, where cross-species or wrong-genotype reads measure contamination directly. They should be scored with this same metric suite, with the official SoupX, DecontX (celda), and CellBender as comparators. read_10x_counts() and split_droplets() now get such data in. Wrappers for the official SoupX, DecontX, FastCAR and CellBender are in validation/comparators.R; so far only the SoupX one has been run.

Development 

devtools::test()            # unit tests: guarantees, sparse==dense, calibration, I/O
devtools::check()           # R CMD check (clean as of v0.2)
Rscript run_all_gates.R     # the scientific scorecard

CI runs R CMD check on Linux/macOS/Windows and the gate scorecard on every PR, and fails if the rho gate stops passing.
